name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
what_is_it: A comprehensive automated laboratory blood panel that evaluates the primary cellular components of blood.
why_is_it_performed: To evaluate overall health, detect infections, diagnose anemia, assess clotting ability, and monitor ongoing treatments.
what_does_it_measure: Red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC), hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelet counts.
what_does_result_represent: Numbers and proportions of circulating blood cells compared to healthy reference intervals.
important_limitations: Does not identify specific causes of illness on its own; abnormal counts require clinical context, history, and examination.
source: American Association for Clinical Chemistry (AACC) / MedlinePlus

name: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c)
what_is_it: A blood test measuring the percentage of hemoglobin bound to glucose over red blood cell lifespan.
why_is_it_performed: To screen for, diagnose, and monitor long-term control of diabetes and prediabetes.
what_does_it_measure: Average blood sugar control over the past 2 to 3 months.
what_does_result_represent: Values below 5.7% are normal; 5.7% to 6.4% indicate prediabetes; 6.5% or higher on two separate occasions indicates diabetes according to ADA criteria.
important_limitations: Conditions altering RBC turnover (like hemolytic anemia, recent blood transfusion, hemoglobin variants) can artificially skew values.
source: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care

name: Fasting Blood Glucose
what_is_it: A blood test measuring circulating glucose levels after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours.
why_is_it_performed: To detect hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, and assess acute glucose regulation.
what_does_it_measure: Concentration of free glucose circulating in venous plasma (mg/dL or mmol/L).
what_does_result_represent: Normal fasting level is typically 70-99 mg/dL; 100-125 mg/dL indicates impaired fasting glucose; 126 mg/dL or higher suggests diabetes.
important_limitations: Represents glucose at a single moment in time; influenced by acute stress, medications, recent food intake, or infection.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)

name: Lipid Profile Panel
what_is_it: A panel of blood tests that measures specific fat molecules circulating in the bloodstream.
why_is_it_performed: To assess cardiovascular risk, screen for hyperlipidemia, and guide preventative cardiovascular therapies.
what_does_it_measure: Total cholesterol, High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL), Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL), and Triglycerides.
what_does_result_represent: Higher LDL is associated with increased plaque risk; higher HDL provides protective cardiovascular clearance.
important_limitations: Individual cardiovascular risk depends on multiple factors including age, smoking, blood pressure, and diabetes, not just isolated numbers.

name: C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
what_is_it: A blood test measuring an acute-phase reactant protein synthesized rapidly by the liver.
why_is_it_performed: To detect and monitor active inflammation, acute bacterial infections, tissue injury, or autoimmune flare-ups.
what_does_it_measure: Concentration of CRP in the serum (mg/L).
what_does_result_represent: Elevations signal presence of systemic inflammation somewhere in the body.
important_limitations: Non-specific; elevated CRP indicates inflammation is present but does not pinpoint the exact location or underlying cause.

name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
what_is_it: A test measuring the rate at which red blood cells settle to the bottom of a vertical tube over one hour.
why_is_it_performed: To help detect non-specific systemic inflammation associated with infections, malignancies, or autoimmune diseases.
what_does_it_measure: Millimeters of cleared plasma settled in one hour (mm/hr).
what_does_result_represent: Higher sedimentation rates correlate with increased inflammatory proteins in plasma.
important_limitations: A non-specific marker influenced by age, gender, pregnancy, and anemia; cannot diagnose a specific disease alone.

name: Liver Function Tests (LFT Panel)
what_is_it: A group of biochemical blood tests measuring liver enzymes, proteins, and bilirubin.
why_is_it_performed: To screen for liver damage, monitor hepatitis or medication toxicity, and evaluate jaundice or abdominal symptoms.
what_does_it_measure: ALT, AST, Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP), Total Bilirubin, Direct Bilirubin, Albumin, and Total Protein.
what_does_result_represent: Integrity of hepatocyte membranes, biliary excretion efficiency, and liver synthetic capacity.
important_limitations: Elevations do not always mean permanent liver damage; temporary elevations frequently occur with mild viral infections or medications.

name: Kidney Function Tests (KFT Panel)
what_is_it: A panel of serum blood and electrolyte tests evaluating how effectively the kidneys filter metabolic waste.
why_is_it_performed: To evaluate renal filtration, screen for acute or chronic kidney disease, and monitor medication clearance.
what_does_it_measure: Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) / Urea, and estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR).
what_does_result_represent: Higher creatinine and urea levels with reduced eGFR indicate decreased renal filtration capacity.
important_limitations: Serum creatinine can vary with muscle mass, dehydration, high-protein diet, and specific medications without true kidney injury.

name: Serum Creatinine
what_is_it: Measurement of a normal metabolic byproduct of muscle creatine breakdown.
why_is_it_performed: Primary laboratory indicator for estimating kidney filtration capacity.
what_does_it_measure: Concentration of creatinine in milligrams per deciliter (mg/dL).
what_does_result_represent: Healthy kidneys maintain creatinine within an expected reference range by constant excretion.
important_limitations: Must be evaluated alongside age, sex, and weight to calculate an accurate estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

name: Urea / Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
what_is_it: Measurement of nitrogenous waste derived from protein digestion in the liver.
why_is_it_performed: To evaluate kidney function, hydration status, and protein metabolism.
what_does_it_measure: Amount of urea or urea nitrogen circulating in serum (mg/dL).
what_does_result_represent: High levels may reflect reduced renal excretion, dehydration, gastrointestinal bleeding, or very high protein intake.
important_limitations: Heavily influenced by hydration and dietary protein; less specific for isolated renal injury than creatinine.

name: Total & Direct Bilirubin
what_is_it: Measurement of yellow pigment resulting from normal breakdown of red blood cell heme.
why_is_it_performed: To diagnose jaundice, liver diseases, biliary obstruction, or excessive red cell breakdown (hemolysis).
what_does_it_measure: Total bilirubin and conjugated (direct) bilirubin levels in serum (mg/dL).
what_does_result_represent: Elevated bilirubin causes visible yellow discoloration of sclera and skin (jaundice).
important_limitations: Does not determine cause alone; fractionating into direct vs indirect is required to distinguish hemolysis from liver or biliary obstruction.
